newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand bank bills close on 9.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand bank bills close on 9.0 percent.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
* Bank bills end at 9.0 percent, first time since April
* Bonds seen taking lead from U.S., trend for yields down
New Zealand short-term yields closed around 9.0 percent on Friday, the first time they have fallen to this level since April.
Dealers said yields were encouraged lower by the firmer currency which regained 40 basis points following its near one cent fall on Thursday.
They said the Reserve Bank statement on Thursday has sanctioned a fall in yields as long as it is accompanied by a rise in the currency.
There was whippy trade in the bond market.
"There were rumours of sellers but price action suggests that there were more buyers than sellers," said one dealer.
Another said the local market is likely to be initially directed by the U.S. market but in the medium-term there was little doubt which way yields would go.
"I think the trend for yields is lower over time, make no mistake," he said.
However, another dealer said the bond market was vulnerable to profit taking from foreign holders who dominate supply.
"The back end looks vulnerable given investors have had super-normal profits in recent weeks," he said.
Rumours of further euro issues refuse to die and that is likely to keep the market underpinned.
In the background will be political talks about the formation of a government following the inconclusive October 12 election.

Dealers said the market had priced in the formation of a government between the ruling conservative National Party and the king-making New Zealand First, but if NZ First goes with left-of-centre Labour they do not see a heavy sell-off.
